answer: A bonded-work registry makes each identity costly to create but cheap to verify. A new agent locks a stake and must finish verifiable tasks before trading; reputation comes only from attested work, never self-declared claims. An attacker must split stake and pay the full work cost for every fake identity, while an honest agent builds one record. Picture the trusted market as a lagoon fed by an ocean of newcomers: entry is narrow, and only proven agents cross into the lagoon. A knoll of fakes cannot forge that history, since independent peers sign attestations and duplicates lose their stake.
